'''Roberto Longo''' (born 9 May 1953) is an Italian mathematician, specializing in [[operator algebra]]s and [[quantum field theory]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Roberto Longo|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Rome Tor Vergata|url=http://www.mat.uniroma2.it/longo/|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Roberto Longo graduated in Mathematics<ref>The academic degree is ''[[Laurea]] in Matematica'' and was the highest academic title at the epoch.</ref> at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1975 under the supervision of the mathematical physicist [[Sergio Doplicher]].<ref>The thesis is {{cite thesis|last=Longo|first=Roberto|date=1975|title=Tomita-Takesaki modular structure for AFD von Neumann algebras|place=Rome}} {{MathGenealogy|id=100244}}</ref> From 1975 to 1977 Longo was a [[predoctoral fellow]] of the [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]] and later [[assistant professor]] at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he became an [[associate professor]] in 1980. In 1987, he was nominated [[full professor]] of [[functional analysis]] at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]], and since 2010, he has been the director of the [[Center for Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] in Rome.

Between 1978 and 1979, he was [[visiting scholar]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. He has been a [[visiting professor]] in numerous research centers, including the [[CNRS]] in [[Marseille]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]], the [[Harvard University]], [[MIT]], and the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Roberto Longo, Curriculum Vitae|website=University of Rome Tor Vergara|url=http://www.mat.uniroma2.it/longo/Home_files/CV-2010.pdf|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref>

Since 2024, Roberto Longo has been an Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]].

Longo is an expert in the theory of operator algebras and its applications to quantum field theory. His work influenced the structural analysis of quantum field theory, especially of [[conformal field theory]], and opened up to new developments in model-building methods of interest in [[local quantum physics]].<ref name=Humboldt>{{cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrview%5BpPersonId%5D=1154986&cHash=13869c9b9202d59fc4928bef1b780146|title=Humboldt Foundation member page of Roberto Longo|website=humboldt-foundation.de|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref>

Roberto Longo is known in particular for his work with Sergio Doplicher on split inclusions of [[von Neumann algebra]]s<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=S.|last2=Longo|first2=R.|title=Standard and split inclusions of von Neumann algebras|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=75|issue=3|year=1984|pages=493–536|issn=0020-9910|doi=10.1007/BF01388641|url=https://eudml.org/doc/143108|bibcode=1984InMat..75..493D|s2cid=121819323|url-access=subscription|hdl=2108/53288|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and for having solved, independently with [[Sorin Popa]], the Stone-Weierstrass conjecture for factorial states.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Longo|first=Roberto|title=Solution of the factorial Stone-Weierstrass conjecture. An application of the theory of standard split W*-inclusions|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=76|number=1|year=1984|pages=145–155|doi=10.1007/BF01388497|bibcode=1984InMat..76..145L|s2cid=122775835}}</ref> He also found the relationship between the statistical dimension<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Doplicher|first1=Sergio|last2=Haag|first2=Rudolf|last3=Roberts|first3=John E.|title=Local observables and particle statistics. 1|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=23|pages=199–230|year=1971|issue=3|doi=10.1007/BF01877742|bibcode=1971CMaPh..23..199D|s2cid=189833852|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1103857630 }}</ref> and the Jones index.<ref>{{cite journal|arxiv=funct-an/9604008|last1=Longo|first1=Roberto|last2=Roberts|first2=John E.|title=A Theory of Dimension|journal=K-Theory|year=1997|volume=11|issue=2|pages=103–159|doi=10.1023/A:1007714415067|bibcode = 1996funct.an..4008L|s2cid=119581477}}</ref> In a work with Yasuyuki Kawahigashi, Longo classified the discrete series of conformal chiral networks of von Neumann algebras.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Classification of local conformal nets: Case c < 1|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=160|pages=493–522|year=2004|last1=Kawahigashi|first1=Yasuyuki|last2=Longo|first2=Roberto|issue=2|doi=10.4007/annals.2004.160.493|arxiv=math-ph/0201015|s2cid=7145642}}</ref> Together with Vincenzo Morinelli and Karl-Henning Rehren, he also showed that particles with infinite spin cannot appear in a local theory.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Longo|first1=Roberto|last2=Morinelli|first2=Vincenzo|last3=Rehren|first3=Karl-Henning|title=Where Infinite Spin Particles Are Localizable|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=345|year=2016|issue=2|pages=587–614|doi=10.1007/s00220-015-2475-9|arxiv=1505.01759|bibcode=2016CMaPh.345..587L|s2cid=119569712}}</ref> His most recent works concern [[entropy]] and [[information theory|information]] for infinite [[quantum system]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ciolli|first1=Fabio|last2=Longo|first2=Roberto|last3=Ruzzi|first3=Giuseppe|title=The information in a wave|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|volume=379|year=2019|issue=3|pages=979–1000|doi=10.1007/s00220-019-03593-3|arxiv=1906.01707|bibcode=2019CMaPh.379..979C|s2cid=174799030}}</ref>

== Honours and awards ==
In 1994 Longo was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|website=mathunion.org|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=longo|access-date=February 19, 2021}} {{cite book|author=Longo, Roberto|chapter=Von Neumann algebras and quantum field theory|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1994, Zürich|volume=2|pages=1281–1291|year=1995}}</ref> He was invited speaker at the [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]] in 1981 in [[Berlin]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Longo, Roberto|chapter=Modular Automorphisms of Local Algebras in Quantum Field Theory|title=6th International Conference on Mathematical Physics - Congress of Association for Mathematical Physics|pages=372–373|year=1981|place=Berlin}}</ref> in 1988 in [[Swansea]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Longo, Roberto|chapter=Inclusions of Von Neumann Algebrass and Quantum Field Theory|title=IX International Conference on Mathematical Physics (IAMP)|pages=472–474|year=1988|place=Swansea}}</ref> in 1994 in [[Paris]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Longo, Roberto|chapter=Inclusions of von Neumann algebras and superselection structures|title=11th International Conference on Mathematical Physics (ICMP-11)|place=Paris|pages=342–351|year=1994}}</ref> and in 2003 in [[Lisbon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ICMP 2003 schedule|website=XIV ICMP Lisbon|url=http://icmp2003.net/schedule/|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref> In 2004 he was Andrejewski Lecturer in Göttingen.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mathematisches Institut - Andrejewski Vorlesung|website=uni-math.gwdg.de|url=https://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/andrej/longo.html|access-date=February 23, 2021|language=de|archive-date=September 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220910094410/https://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/andrej/longo.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a plenary speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in 2009 in [[Prague]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Plenary Speakers|website=ICMP Prague|url=http://icmp.ujf.cas.cz/confirmed-plenary-speakers.htm|access-date=February 19, 2021|archive-date=August 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816194742/http://icmp.ujf.cas.cz/confirmed-plenary-speakers.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> and at ''Strings 2018'' in [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Modular theory and Bekenstein's bound'' by Robert Longo, partly based on a joint work with Feng Xu|website=Okinawa, OIST, Strings 2018|url=https://indico.oist.jp/indico/event/5/picture/116.pdf|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref>

In 2013 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#d|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|website=American Mathematical Society|access-date=February 19, 2021}} {{cite journal|last=Jackson|first=Allyn|title=Fellows of the AMS: Inaugural Class|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=60|number=5|year=2013|pages=631–637|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/rnoti-p631.pdf}}</ref> and in 2021 a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Longo_Roberto|title=Longo's member page of Academia Europæa|website=Academia Europæa|access-date=July 20, 2021}}</ref> He was awarded in 2016 the [[Humboldt Research Award]]<ref name=Humboldt/><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Humboldt-Preisträger|journal=Uni Inform, Göttingen|date=April 2015|page=5|language=de}}</ref> 
and in 2021 the XL medal from the [[Accademia Nazionale delle Scienze detta dei XL]] for his in-depth and innovative research in operator algebras and in conformal field theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.uniroma2.it/module/name/Content/newlang/italiano/navpath/HOM/action/showpage/content_id/94622|title=A Roberto Longo la Medaglia dei XL per la Matematica 2021|website=uniroma2.it|language=it|access-date=July 20, 2021}}</ref> In 2013 the conference ''Mathematics and Quantum Physics'' at the [[Lincei National Academy]] was dedicated to him on the occasion of his 60th birthday.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cmtp.uniroma2.it/13MQP/|title=Mathematics and Quantum Physics Conference|website=cmtp.uniroma2.it|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref> In 2008<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Scienze, Roma trionfa negli Advanced grants|journal = Il Sole 24 Ore, Roma|number = 40|date = October 15, 2008|language=it}} {{cite web|title=Advanced Grants: Operator Algebras and Conformal Field Theory|website=europa.eu|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/227458|access-date=February 25, 2021}}</ref> and in 2015<ref>{{cite web|title=Advanced Grants: Quantum Algebraic Structures and Models|website=europa.eu|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/669240|access-date=February 25, 2021}}</ref> he received two [[European Research Council#Advanced Grants|Advanced Grants]] from the [[European Research Council]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Un matematico di Tor Vergata vincitore dell'"Advanced Grants"|website=maddmaths.simai.eu|url=http://maddmaths.simai.eu/news-2/roberto-longo-si-aggiudica-il-suo-secondo-erc-con-un-progetto-su-matematica-e-fisica-quantistica/|access-date=February 23, 2021|language=it}}</ref> In 2018 he was member of the sectional panel ''Mathematical Physics'' of the International Congress of Mathematicians in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/IMU/ICM2018/Panelists_2018.pdf|title=Sectional Panels for ICM 2018|website=mathunion.org/icm/past-icms|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref>
